scenes.headline: colour receptor types in some mantis shrimp eyes
Who has the most colour channels?

scenes.label: it's worse than you at telling similar colours apart

scenes.headline: It recognises colours fast instead of comparing them.
scenes.body: Scientists think it scans its eyes across objects and reads all 12 channels at once.

caption:
12 colour channels and still bad at shades.

In tests, mantis shrimp struggled to tell apart colours that humans separate easily. The best explanation: their eyes are built for quick colour recognition, not fine comparison.

Source: Thoen et al. 2014, Science; Journal of Experimental Biology review (2022).  Photos/video: Wikimedia Commons (credits on screen).
notes: Animated myth-flip: the chart sets up the 'super-vision' myth, the stat card overturns it with the actual 2014 finding. All graphics, one macro photo.
